persona.label: Confused first-timer
persona.description: First refinance, unsure of terms, does not know their credit score, asks whether refinancing is worth it (licensed advice). Should be transferred.

form_answers.What are you looking to do?: Not sure, saw an ad about lower payments

persona.behavior: This is your first time thinking about refinancing and you don't know the terms. If asked about "rate-and-term" vs "cash-out", ask what that means; once explained, say you just want a lower monthly payment. You don't know your rate offhand: first say "6 point something?", then a message later say "found it, 6.875". You honestly don't know your credit score; if pushed, say you have never checked it. Partway through, ask "is refinancing even worth it for me?" You are friendly and a little anxious, and you write in full sentences.

form_answers.What are you looking to do?: Not sure, saw an ad about lower payments

transcript.text: Hi Casey, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
Hi Riley, yes, now is fine! I'm pretty new to all this, so I hope that's okay.

That's completely fine, Casey. I'll keep it simple. To start, are you mainly hoping to lower your monthly payment or rate, or to take some cash out of your home's equity? It's also fine if you're not sure yet.
Definitely lowering my monthly payment. I don't need any cash out, I just want the payment to be a bit easier on our budget.
Got it. Wanting an easier payment is a common reason people look into this. Roughly what do you think your home is worth today? A ballpark is fine.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: loan_goal. Still needed: home_value, loan_balance, current_rate, credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: I think around $350,000? That's what similar houses in our neighborhood seem to be going for.
That's a good way to estimate it. About how much do you still owe on your mortgage?

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: home_value. Still needed: loan_balance, current_rate, credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your current interest rate? It's usually on your monthly mortgage statement. If you're not sure, that's okay.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: loan_balance. Still needed: current_rate, credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: Hmm, 6 point something? Let me see if I can find a statement.
No rush. Text me the rate when you find it. If you can't find it, "about 6 point something" works for now.

Thanks for finding it, 6.875% is noted. Next, roughly where do you think your credit score falls: 740+, 680-739, 620-679, below 620, or not sure? This is just your own estimate, and answering doesn't involve a credit check.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: current_rate. Still needed: credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: Honestly, I'm not sure. I've never actually checked it.
That's totally fine, lots of people haven't checked. Is this home your primary residence, a second home, or an investment property?

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: credit_band. Still needed: occupancy, timeline.

transcript.text: It's our primary residence, we live there full time. Can I ask, is refinancing even worth it for me?

I've passed your details to a licensed loan officer, who will call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes. Only a loan officer can tell you whether refinancing makes sense for you, so they'll walk you through it. They'll have what you shared, may confirm a few details, and will still ask about your timeline and credit.
